claims.text: microduck-cli sets up a MicroDuck environment (sim or real), trains and publishes policies through microduck_rl, drives the duck directly over robotd's JSON-RPC, and runs a data-only rules layer (events -> rules -> actions) — one CLI that any agent or human drives, implementing the upstream pollen-robotics docs and pointing users at them.

honesty_conditions.text: The announcement is true only if every operate verb works unchanged against BOTH 'robotd --fake' (CI) and 'robotd --sim' (MuJoCo) through the same socket client — no sim-specific code path above the transport seam.

claims.instruction: Verify by running the same 'duck' verbs against a --fake daemon in tests and a --sim daemon on the dev box; implement by keeping robot control behind one JSON-RPC client seam and one engine TargetSink, with sim vs real being only a socket path.

claims.text: No code is copied, vendored or cited from pollen-robotics/microduck or microduck_rl. The CLI implements against their documented surfaces — robotctl/duckctl verbs (docs/robot/cheatsheet.md, duckctl.md), the JSON-RPC method names in duck-ipc-proto/src/lib.rs, and microduck_rl's 'uv run train/play/publish' + scripts/export.py — and links users to those docs rather than restating them.

No motor is ever commanded except as an intent through robotd's JSON-RPC (robot.move/head/look/do/init/relax/stop/setMode/loadPolicy). robotd is authoritative on safety (architecture.md §1.1 invariant 2: fall detection, joint/thermal limits, deadman, safe pose) and is the only process on the Dynamixel bus; microduck-cli never opens the serial port, never bypasses a clamp, and treats a refused intent as the correct answer.

honesty_conditions.text: A grep of microduck_cli/ finds no serial-port open, no Dynamixel/rustypot import and no write to /dev/tty*; every motion path ends in a JSON-RPC call, and a refused intent is reported by the daemon's reason code with exit 0 for the engine and exit 1 for a verb.

claims.text: Transport is JSON-RPC 2.0 NDJSON over robotd's unix socket, implemented with stdlib socket+json only. The socket path is configurable (--socket / DUCK_SOCKET): in simulation it is the short state-dir path robotd --sim was started with (upstream's scripts/duck-sim uses $DUCK_SIM_STATE/duck-a.sock; a unix path is capped at ~108 bytes), and when a real duck exists the same client points at a forwarded /run/robotd.sock ('ssh -L …', cheatsheet-dev.md). Method names, API_VERSION, the 'hello' handshake, error codes and JOINT_NAMES come from duck-ipc-proto/src/lib.rs and are re-checked at connect. Continuous intents (robot.move/head/pose/mouth/sound hold) are sent as notifications at 20–50 Hz, last-writer-wins and expiring; discrete ones (robot.do/look/stop/enable/init/relax) as answered requests — the split the proto crate documents.

honesty_conditions.text: A daemon answering hello with a newer API_VERSION runs; an unknown method answers METHOD_NOT_FOUND and is logged as a named drop, never a traceback; a daemon whose JOINT_NAMES or obs/action lengths differ from the client's table refuses to start the engine with both numbers in the message.

revisions.text: Real-duck transport is JSON-RPC 2.0 over robotd's unix socket, reached from a laptop through the documented forward 'ssh -L /tmp/robotd.sock:/run/robotd.sock radxa@<ip>' (cheatsheet-dev.md 'From a laptop — drive with a pad in your hands'), or natively when the CLI runs on the board. Implemented with stdlib socket+json only; method names, API_VERSION (23 today), the 'hello' handshake, error codes and JOINT_NAMES are taken from duck-ipc-proto/src/lib.rs and re-checked at connect, never assumed.
revisions.reason: no physical duck yet; sim daemon runs on this host

claims.text: Addressing follows upstream's simulation naming: a duck is a name (duck-a, duck-b …) that resolves to <state-dir>/<name>.sock (and <name>-tof.sock), the convention scripts/duck-sim establishes; DUCK_SIM_DUCK / --duck select one. duckctl (BLE, 'never on a robot') is wrapped only when a real duck exists — it is not a sim transport. The env doctor names exactly what is missing for the sim stack (a microduck clone on sim-remote-io, cargo/rust ≥1.89, a built robotd+robotctl, a microduck_rl .venv with libonnxruntime, a short state dir, a free body port) with the upstream doc line as the remediation.

honesty_conditions.text: Given a state dir and a name, the CLI resolves <state>/<name>.sock without any network or BLE call; env doctor on a box with no microduck clone, no cargo, no RL venv or no libonnxruntime lists each missing item with the upstream doc line and exits 2.

revisions.text: Discovery and addressing follow duckctl's conventions: DUCK_ROBOT names the robot, 'duckctl scan'/'duckctl ip' (BLE, Rust, built with 'cargo run -p duckctl' from the upstream clone) yield the IPv4 the CLI then ssh-forwards to. The CLI wraps duckctl when present, otherwise takes --host / a DUCK_HOST env, and its env doctor names exactly what is missing (cargo, duckctl build, ssh key on the board, hf auth, CUDA GPU) with the upstream doc link as the remediation.

claims.text: The operate surface uses robotctl's words so a command learned on the robot works here: robot init/relax/do/mode/look, policy list/load/add/remove/reset/search/check/update, pad status/bindings/bind/reset, health, monitor (--json NDJSON), configure --list, quack. It adds one verb robotctl lacks — a velocity 'move' driving robot.move with the deadman refreshed at intent rate, the way padd and the WebRTC console do — and every verb takes --json.

honesty_conditions.text: Every verb name and flag in the duck noun matches a robotctl subcommand of the same name (robot init/relax/do/mode/look, policy *, pad *, health, monitor, configure --list, quack) plus exactly one addition, move; a table test pins that list against robotctl's Namespace enum.

claims.text: Every verb that moves or de-energizes the duck is gated the arm101 way: confirm on a TTY, print a zero-side-effect dry-run plan on a non-TTY without --apply, proceed on a non-TTY with --apply (agent mode). Applies to init, relax (which additionally keeps upstream's --yes semantics), do, move, mode, policy load/add/reset, and pad bind. Upstream's own safety wording is surfaced verbatim: 'init moves every joint — have the robot on its stand', 'relax cuts power and the robot collapses', 'stop zeroes intents and is NOT an emergency stop', 'nothing a stranger publishes is verified by anybody'.

honesty_conditions.text: Each gated verb has three tests: TTY without --apply prompts, non-TTY without --apply prints a plan and sends nothing (asserted on a --fake daemon's call log), non-TTY with --apply sends; the four upstream safety sentences appear verbatim in the verb's dry-run output.

claims.text: The teach/train lane orchestrates microduck_rl by its documented commands, never by importing it: env check (CUDA GPU, uv, Python 3.12 (<3.13 pinned by bam), UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT=600 on ARM, hf auth, optional wandb), 'uv run list-envs', the mandatory 64-env/5-iter smoke test, 'uv run train <task> [--hf-jobs]', 'uv run play', 'uv run scripts/export.py' (the only safe ONNX path — normalizer baked in), 'uv run publish' (schema-2 manifest, [1,61]->[1,14] gate), then 'robotctl policy add|load' on the duck. The CLI plans and sequences that pipeline, records the artifacts (task id, run path, checkpoint, ONNX, HF repo), and points at AGENTS.md for reward design.

honesty_conditions.text: The train lane never imports mjlab_microduck; each stage is a subprocess whose argv equals the upstream-documented command, and the lane refuses to start a long run whose 64-env/5-iteration smoke test has not passed in this session or a recorded artifact.

claims.text: microduck_rl is orchestrated as a sibling checkout via subprocess ('uv run --project <path> …'), never added as a dependency or extra of microduck-cli: its dependency tree (mjlab, warp, torch+CUDA, bam from git, requires-python <3.13) must not enter this package's resolution. Base runtime deps stay [] (CLAUDE.md hard constraint); if a hardware library is ever needed it goes behind an extra with a lazy import.

honesty_conditions.text: pyproject.toml dependencies stays []; a CI check fails if it is non-empty or if any [project.optional-dependencies] entry names mjlab, warp-lang, torch or better-actuator-models.

claims.text: No training code lives here: no env cfgs, reward functions, MDP terms, MJCF models, exporters or publishers. Those are microduck_rl's (src/mjlab_microduck/tasks, export.py, publish/); the CLI wraps, sequences and explains them. Likewise no policy files are bundled — policies come from the Hub (pollen-robotics/microduck-policies or a community repo) or the trainer's own export.

Sim-through-the-daemon is available today by building the microduck 'sim-remote-io' branch: docs/design/simulation.md on that branch reports 'working end to end for one duck' — robotd holds 50.0 of 50.0 Hz against a MuJoCo body, detects a seated boot, and 'robotctl robot init' stands the duck up. The stack is: microduck_rl 'uv run duck-body [--ducks N --port 7801 --headless]' + 'robotd --sim 127.0.0.1:7801 --socket <short path> --params <generated toml>' (ort dlopens libonnxruntime from the RL venv; policies are named in the params file) + robotctl/our CLI on that socket. 'robotd --fake' (a robot made of nothing, no physics) is the CI-grade backend. Risks: the branch is 32 ahead / 87 behind main and unmerged; containers, ether, camera and ToF are 'designed and measured but not built'. scripts/infer_policy.py remains the no-daemon fallback.

revisions.text: Two simulation paths exist upstream today and they are not equivalent: (a) 'uv run scripts/infer_policy.py --walking out.onnx' — CPU MuJoCo with BAM actuators, keyboard-driven, no daemon — usable now for rehearsal; (b) 'uv run duck-body' (microduck_rl develop, TCP NDJSON body server) + 'robotd --sim 127.0.0.1:7801' — the daemon half exists only on microduck branch 'sim-remote-io', not main, so 'the same robotctl/JSON-RPC surface against sim and real' is upstream-pending. The CLI's env doctor reports which path is available rather than assuming (b).

claims.text: The rules layer follows reachy-mini-cli's shape: data-only TOML — [[react]] (when <predicate> then run <action>), [[inhibit]], [modes.<name>] — predicates as field/op/value over a sense snapshot (never code), unique ids, cooldown_s, hysteresis, bounded duration_s, two-layer per-id merge (shipped resource + box-local overlay with 'enabled = false' tombstones), fail-closed validation, and 'rules list/check/overview' verbs. Duck sense fields are derived from robot.state / robot.health / pad.input / tof.frame / chorale.heard (fallen, projected gravity, battery fraction, hottest servo, loop Hz, pad buttons, ToF nearest, nearby-duck beacons); actions are robotd intents (do <skill>, look, move, sound/quack, stop, mode).

honesty_conditions.text: RulesConfig.from_dict refuses every documented bad shape (unknown field, callable value, unknown skill, unknown predicate field/op, negative cooldown, duplicate id, unbounded looping) with the rule id in the message; a two-layer merge test proves per-id override and enabled=false tombstones survive an upgrade of the shipped layer.

claims.text: No 50 Hz tick loop, channel arbitration, sense driver or TickBus is implemented in microduck_cli/. That runtime belongs in neurosymbolic-system (tick_seam, SenseProviders, TargetSink, rules-as-data) and is imported once it ships; until then this repo lands the rules schema, the loader/validator, the duck sense-field and action vocabularies, and dry-run evaluation against a recorded robot.state stream. Anything engine-shaped that appears here is filed upstream instead.

No language model sits inside the rules layer's decision path. Agents (any backend) drive the CLI from outside — authoring rules, choosing skills, starting training — and the rules evaluator stays symbolic and model-free, machine-checkable the way reachy-mini-cli's tests/test_zero_llm_boundary.py checks it.

Upstream's autonomous brain is unported: roadmap M9 says the prototype's autonomous.rs (in the private microduck_runtime, not a public repo) 'exists nowhere in the daemon' and it 'gets a design doc before it gets code'. So today the daemon offers policies, skills, safety and intents but no idle behaviour. The rules layer + engine in this repo therefore IS the duck's off-board behaviour for now, sending intents robotd may refuse; when M9 lands, the engine's rules become a layer above upstream's brain (inputs: chorale beacons/RSSI, ToF, sound events) rather than its replacement — the seam is the intent API either way.

revisions.text: Upstream's own autonomy — a 16-state behavior machine (Chill/Wander/Zoomies/Startle/Nap/BallPlay/Petted…) with mood, novelty-grid exploration and ToF avoidance — is a holding pen (docs/ideas/autonomous_behavior.md) with no design doc and no daemon code yet. The rules layer here is complementary: operator-authored, data-only, off-board, sending intents robotd may refuse — not a port of that state machine and not a competitor for robotd's loop. When upstream's brain lands, rules become a policy over its inputs rather than a replacement.
revisions.reason: user wants the duck as autonomous as upstream makes it, with our rules layer above

claims.text: The development box is a DGX Spark GB10 (linux-aarch64, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.126) — exactly the ARM configuration microduck_rl documents (torch cu129 index, UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT=600 on first sync). hf auth is present (user orinachum), cargo/rustc are installed (duckctl is buildable), Python 3.12 is available via uv. Not present: a wandb ~/.netrc, any DUCK_ROBOT/DUCK_HOST setting, a duck in Bluetooth range or ssh config — so 'we have a duck, a communication with it' is not yet observable from this machine and the address/transport must come from the user.

There is no Radxa board and no physical duck yet. The target is the SIMULATED duck: microduck_rl's 'duck-body' (MuJoCo) driven by the real 'robotd --sim' from the microduck 'sim-remote-io' branch, reached over robotd's unix socket exactly as a real duck would be. duckctl is not the transport — it is a BLE client for a real duck's btd and has no equivalent in sim; the CLI talks JSON-RPC to robotd's socket directly.

microduck-cli implements its own engine, following reachy-mini-cli's seams (one 50 Hz-class tick, tick_seam/TickBus fan-out, SenseProviders as injected peek callables, a TargetSink, rules as data, one admission registry for rule-fired and agent-injected intents, heartbeat-based liveness, named senselog drops). The duck stays as autonomous as upstream makes it, and this engine is a rules layer ABOVE it that injects instructions; an agent can inject ad-hoc instructions through the same path or author rules that do. neurosymbolic-system is then built by extracting from BOTH reachy-mini-cli and this engine, and this repo refactors to import it. This supersedes the CLAUDE.md line that says an engine loop here belongs upstream.

Training runs locally OR on Hugging Face Jobs, selectable per run. Local targets to support: DGX Spark (GB10), Jetson Thor, and Jetson AGX Orin. wandb is optional and configurable — never required for the lane to work.

The env noun brings up and checks the simulation stack by reproducing upstream's documented steps (or shelling out to scripts/duck-sim when the clone has it): clone/checkout microduck at sim-remote-io, 'cargo build -p robotd -p robotctl -p tof -p sounds', locate libonnxruntime in the microduck_rl .venv, generate a params toml naming the policy files from the clone, start 'duck-body' on a port then 'robotd --sim host:port --socket <state>/<name>.sock', wait for 'hello' + robot.health, and optionally 'robot.init'. It supports N ducks (one port each, one MuJoCo world), a scene (bare floor or apartment), headless mode, and a --fake backend for tests; 'env down' stops by pidfile after confirming /proc cmdline (upstream's stop_one lesson), never by name.

honesty_conditions.text: env up on a box with the two clones and a synced RL venv reaches robot.health healthy within 60 s on --fake and within 120 s on --sim; env down leaves no robotd, duck-body or tofd process and never signals a pid whose /proc cmdline does not match.

claims.text: The engine package (microduck_cli/behavior/ or engine/) mirrors reachy-mini-cli's shape so it can be extracted: engine.run(tick_seam=…) with a TickBus of drivers; a pure data model (channels, StopClass priorities, Lifetime) with duck channels = the intent families robotd exposes (twist, head, body pose, mouth, sound, skill); SenseProviders fed from robot.subscribe/robot.state + robot.health polled at 2 Hz + tof.frame + chorale.heard (peek callables, *_age_s freshness, None on failure); a TargetSink that emits intents through the JSON-RPC client; rules-as-data loaded in two layers; bounded lifetimes fail-closed; senselog drop reasons on stderr; a state.json heartbeat so a second engine process refuses early. honesty_conditions.text: The engine adds no command filtering of its own: robotd's cmd_alpha/head_alpha EMA (0.2 default in deploy/robotd.toml) is treated as part of the plant, so a rule's step command arrives as the ramp the daemon documents.

claims.text: Instruction injection has ONE admission path: a KindRegistry-style registry that validates fail-closed and admits (a) intents fired by react rules and (b) ad-hoc intents an agent or human sends via a CLI verb (e.g. 'duck intent <kind> …' / a spool file) — same validator, same bounds (duration caps, per-axis limits, cooldowns), same named refusals. Rules are the durable form of an instruction; an ad-hoc intent is the one-shot form. Every admitted instruction becomes robotd intents that robotd's own safety may still refuse, and the refusal is surfaced by name.

honesty_conditions.text: One KindRegistry instance serves both rule-fired and CLI-injected intents: a test injects the same over-limit payload by both paths and gets the same refusal text; a static check finds no second validator.

claims.text: Own what you energize: on any abnormal engine exit (exception, Ctrl-C, socket error) the engine best-effort sends robot.stop, robot.pose {active:false}, robot.mouth 0 and robot.sound hold:false, each independently so one failure does not skip the rest, then exits non-zero naming what it could not send. It does NOT relax the robot (a deliberate hold must survive; relax collapses it). A dead socket is stated as the limit: robotd's own deadman zeroes velocity, but a held pose/mouth outlives us until its notification expires.

honesty_conditions.text: Killing the engine with SIGINT mid-behaviour against a --fake daemon yields exactly stop, pose active:false, mouth 0 and sound hold:false in its call log, no relax, and a non-zero exit naming any release that failed when one is forced to fail.

claims.text: The JSON-RPC client is a background I/O thread pair (writer with a bounded outbound queue; reader correlating replies by id and fanning notifications such as robot.state to peek slots). The tick thread only does put_nowait: a full queue, a wedged socket or a slow daemon resolve to a named drop ('ipc-queue-full', 'ipc-down'), never to a blocked tick. Requests from verbs (do/look/init) wait on their own future with a timeout; notifications are fire-and-forget.

honesty_conditions.text: A test that wedges the fake socket shows the tick period unchanged (measured over 100 ticks) and an ipc-down drop; a test that fills the queue shows an ipc-queue-full drop and no blocked tick.

claims.text: One engine process per duck, addressed by name → socket; N ducks in one MuJoCo world means N engines and N rules overlays. Cross-duck coordination (the chorale's beacons, duck-ether, follow-the-leader) is out of scope for v1 — those inputs arrive later as chorale.heard sense fields, not as a multi-duck engine.

The engine ships one PASSIVE base behaviour (the duck's 'feel-alive': small robot.head / robot.look motions, occasional robot.sound chirps) so a duck with an armed engine is visibly alive between rules; it contributes only while the robot is driving and upright, and any admitted rule behaviour owns its channels over it.

honesty_conditions.text: Idle motion is never sent when robot.state reports fallen, when the robot is not enabled, or while a human is driving; disabling it is a one-line tombstone in the box-local rules overlay.

claims.text: The shipped default rules are few and safety-first, mirroring default_rules.toml's discipline: an inhibit rule that disables every skill and the idle base while robot.state reports fallen (recovery is the daemon's/VelStand policy's job), a low-battery inhibit keyed on robot.health's charge fraction, and at most one or two reactions that are obviously correct in any room. Rule ids are a public interface pinned by a test; everything else is the operator's overlay.

honesty_conditions.text: The shipped rules file contains at most four rules; a test pins their ids; a replay of a recorded fall shows every skill and the idle base inhibited within one tick of fallen=true.

claims.text: No secret ever reaches stdout or a --json payload: HF_TOKEN, wandb keys, DUCK_PIN and the sim's account token file are reported as set/unset by 'env doctor' and never echoed; the train lane passes them by environment to subprocesses, never on a command line (visible in /proc cmdline).

honesty_conditions.text: A test sets HF_TOKEN, DUCK_PIN and a wandb key to sentinel strings and asserts none appears in any stdout, --json or stderr output of env doctor, train or duck verbs, nor in any subprocess argv the lane spawns.

claims.text: 'duck record' captures robot.state (via robot.subscribe), robot.health polls, pad.input and tof.frame to JSONL with monotonic timestamps — the artifact 'rules check --replay' and the engine's offline tests consume, and the source of truth for the duck sense-field vocabulary (resolving the parked unknown about the state payload). Stdout stays pure JSONL; all diagnostics go to stderr.

honesty_conditions.text: duck record against --fake writes one JSON object per line with a monotonic timestamp and source tag; stdout contains nothing but JSONL; rules check --replay accepts that file.

claims.text: rules.toml carries a schema_version; the loader refuses an unknown or missing version fail-closed with the fix named. This is what lets the schema move to neurosymbolic-system later without silently reinterpreting an operator's overlay.

honesty_conditions.text: A rules.toml without schema_version or with an unknown one is refused with the expected version named; the shipped layer and every fixture carry the current version.

claims.text: Human-driving gate (q4, option B): while pad.input or robot.remoteSessionActive shows a human, the engine withholds every body-moving intent (twist, head, look, pose, skills, mode) as a named 'human-driving' drop and keeps the non-motion channels (robot.sound, robot.mouth), recording and rule evaluation live; the engine never overrides a person — robotd's deadman, clamps and fall reflex are the safety layer under a human driver.

open_vagueness.text: robotd --sim (the daemon half of duck-body) has not landed on microduck main — only branch sim-remote-io names it. Sim-through-the-daemon (same JSON-RPC surface as the real duck) is blocked on that merge; infer_policy.py is the only sim available today.
open_vagueness.resolution: Build robotd/robotctl from microduck branch sim-remote-io (working end to end for one duck per its simulation.md); track the merge into main as a follow-up.

open_vagueness.text: neurosymbolic-system has extracted no runtime yet (0.8.0 = bare template). The rules layer's live evaluation on one tick depends on it; the schema/validator/dry-run half does not.
open_vagueness.resolution: Engine implemented in this repo now, extraction-first; neurosymbolic-system is built from reachy-mini-cli + this engine later.

open_vagueness.text: Upstream defers 'a WebSocket surface for server-side programs' (remote-webrtc.md §11: same JSON-RPC, no media stack, get_frame as JPEG). If it lands, the transport layer gains a network path with no ssh; keep the transport behind one seam so it can swap.

The exact robot.state / robot.health payload fields were not read in this pass (robotd/src/{intents,control}.rs, or a captured 'robotctl monitor --json'). The duck sense-field vocabulary for rules must be derived from a real capture, not guessed.

The console-script half-rename (installed 'microduck', internal prog 'microduck-cli') is still open; CLAUDE.md asks for one deliberate pass across pyproject, prog=, _commands, catalog, README and tests. Decide whether it rides with the first duck noun or ships separately first.
sim-remote-io is unmerged (32 ahead / 87 behind main as of 2026-09-03). Pin the exact commit the CLI is validated against and re-check when it merges; API_VERSION and the body protocol (1) may move.

Jetson Thor / AGX Orin: microduck_rl's torch source covers only GB10-class aarch64 (cu129 index); JetPack boards need their own torch/warp builds and mjlab's GPU selection has not been verified there. Unknown until tried on a board.
Whether one engine should ever coordinate several ducks (shared rules, cross-duck events) or whether that always stays per-duck with the mesh as the coordinator.

On a real board, mutating calls need the caller in allow_uids/allow_gids and the socket's 0660 group; a long-running engine process must be provisioned into that (a systemd --user unit like reachy-mini-cli's 'service' noun, or a root-owned unit). Unknown until there is a board; no effect on sim.

Native aarch64 build of robotd/robotctl/tof/sounds from sim-remote-io on this box is unverified (probes: rustc 1.93.1 ≥ 1.89 OK; onnxruntime 1.24.4 ships a cp312 manylinux aarch64 wheel OK). Remaining risk is in the C deps CONTRIBUTING lists for other crates and in warp/mujoco on GB10 for duck-body. Cheap to settle as the first plan task.

scope_entries.surface: pollen-robotics/microduck README + microduck_rl README (user directive: keep originals upstream)
scope_entries.finding: Both repos are Apache-2.0 and actively pushed (2026-09-03); microduck is a Rust workspace of daemons (robotd, updaterd, configd, btd, padd, mediad, tofd) + robotctl/duckctl; microduck_rl is a Python/mjlab training project. Nothing is copied or cited into this repo — the CLI drives their documented commands and protocol and links to their docs.

scope_entries.surface: microduck docs/design/architecture.md (§1.1 invariants, service table)
scope_entries.finding: Seven daemons over one unix socket each, JSON-RPC 2.0 NDJSON; robotd owns motors+safety and never blocks on another service; clients send intents only. Read-only calls are ungated, mutating calls gated by allow_uids/allow_gids + sudo.

scope_entries.surface: microduck docs/robot/cheatsheet-dev.md + duck-ipc-proto/src/lib.rs
scope_entries.finding: The socket-forward path is documented upstream as how padd runs from a clone against a bench robot; the proto crate is the wire contract (API_VERSION 23, POLICY_OBS_LEN 61, POLICY_ACTION_LEN 14, robot.*/policy.*/pad.*/net.*/system.*/update.*/account.* namespaces, robot.subscribe/robot.state stream). A v-skew answers METHOD_NOT_FOUND naming the method, by design.

scope_entries.surface: microduck docs/robot/duckctl.md
scope_entries.finding: duckctl is 'never on a robot', BLE-only today, wraps a subset of the API (info/name/wifi/health/status/version/update/account/policy/do) and broadcasts the robot's IPv4 in its advertisement; 'ssh radxa@$(duckctl ip)' is the documented hop to a shell. Naming: duck-<4 chars from serial>; DUCK_ROBOT/DUCK_PIN env.

scope_entries.surface: microduck robotctl/src/main.rs (Namespace + RobotCommand/PolicyCommand/PadCommand enums) + docs/robot/cheatsheet.md
scope_entries.finding: robotctl's robot namespace is Init/Relax/Do/Mode/Look only — continuous driving comes from padd (gamepad) or the mediad console (WASD at 0.3 m/s, 1.5 rad/s); robotctl exposes stable exit codes CI asserts on (usage, unreachable, busy, refused, not permitted). health exits non-zero when unhealthy so it can gate scripts.

scope_entries.surface: arm101-cli arm101/cli/_commands/{calibrate,set_baudrate}.py + microduck cheatsheet 'Power to the joints' + duckctl.md console notes
scope_entries.finding: arm101 ships the TTY-confirm / dry-run / --apply tri-state and the release-on-abnormal-exit discipline; microduck's docs already carry the exact safety sentences (init, relax --yes, stop is not an e-stop, community policies unverified, robot must be driving for a skill) that the CLI must not soften.

scope_entries.surface: microduck_rl README.md + AGENTS.md + scripts/hf/README.md + pyproject.toml
scope_entries.finding: Console scripts are train/duck-body/publish (list-envs/play come from mjlab); deps are mjlab 1.3.0, warp 1.12, torch 2.9.1 (cu129 index on aarch64), bam from a git branch; requires-python >=3.12,<3.13. AGENTS.md: smoke test first, 61-D obs contract, never hand-convert a checkpoint, budgets 1000-6000 iters at 4096 envs. HF Jobs path: --hf-jobs, flavors l4x1/a10g-large/a100-large, HF_TOKEN + wandb forwarded.

scope_entries.surface: microduck-cli pyproject.toml (dependencies = []) + CLAUDE.md 'Hard constraints' + microduck_rl pyproject.toml
scope_entries.finding: Zero third-party runtime deps is a stated design rule here and in neurosymbolic-system; microduck_rl's pins (~2 GB CUDA wheels, bam git branch, protobuf/onnx/zmq overrides) would break 'uv sync' on a bare box and are out of the question as a dep.

scope_entries.surface: microduck_rl src/mjlab_microduck layout + docs/policy-manifest.md
scope_entries.finding: Publishing contract is schema 2 (kind episodic/perpetual/scripted; command.encoding constant/phase/posture_flag); only constant-command policies are publishable as one-shots; origin (official = pollen-robotics/*, community, local) is decided upstream and drives reset/auto-update behaviour.

scope_entries.surface: microduck_rl src/mjlab_microduck/sim/body_server.py (develop, 2026-08-31) + microduck main tree (no duck-control/src/sim.rs, no --sim in robotd/src/main.rs) + branch list (sim-remote-io)
scope_entries.finding: body_server.py's docstring says 'robotd --sim …' and that 'duck_control::sim is the other end', but that module is absent from main; 'sim-remote-io' is the only upstream branch naming it. Protocol 1, one duck per TCP port, 15 joints on the wire (mouth inserted), TIMESTEP 0.005 with decimation 4 = 50 Hz.

scope_entries.surface: reachy-mini-cli reachy/behavior/{rules.py,default_rules.toml,model.py} + CLAUDE.md 'behavior noun'
scope_entries.finding: rules.py: SENSE_FIELDS/COMPARATORS as frozen sets, RulesConfig.from_dict as the single validation gate, merge_rules per id, MAX_SAY_CHARS fail-closed; default_rules.toml ships only three corroborated rules and documents why rule ids are a public interface. model.py: channels + StopClass priorities + Lifetime — the arbitration core the duck port would need.

scope_entries.surface: neurosymbolic-system CLAUDE.md 'The runtime being extracted' (tick_seam, SenseProviders, 'Rules are data') + microduck-cli CLAUDE.md sibling section
scope_entries.finding: neurosymbolic-system 0.8.0 is still the bare template (cli/ + explain/ only); its brief names the seams the library will define (TargetSink, SenseProviders, speech(text), media_session_provider, start_pose_provider) and says the robot CLI supplies every concrete implementation and holds every client. MicroDuck is explicitly the second robot that forces the seam.

scope_entries.surface: reachy-mini-cli CLAUDE.md 'The zero-LLM boundary — machine-checked'
scope_entries.finding: The donor pins by AST test that behavior/rules/intents/arbitration reach no speech/vision/forge module transitively and that _build_parser() loads no cognition module; cognition survives only behind an explicit agent noun. The same shape (and the accurate wording — 'the decision loop is model-free', not 'contains no LLM') carries over.

scope_entries.surface: microduck docs/ideas/autonomous_behavior.md + docs/README.md ('ideas/ — not designed yet')
scope_entries.finding: The brain is 'the biggest untracked gap'; inputs already exist in the daemon (ambient sound events, depth frames, obstacle points, voice tags, chorale beacons with stable ids and RSSI). Social behaviours are opt-in and off = invisible ([chorale] accept).

scope_entries.surface: microduck-cli microduck_cli/cli/{__init__.py,_commands/cli.py,_commands/overview.py,_commands/doctor.py} + explain/catalog.py + CLAUDE.md 'Architecture'
scope_entries.finding: The chassis has whoami/learn/explain/overview/doctor + the cli noun; _build_parser() has a marked slot for new noun groups; three doc surfaces (catalog, _VERBS, learn) drift silently unless updated together; CI gates on the seven-bundle rubric and coverage fail_under=60.

scope_entries.surface: microduck docs/README.md ('One page owns a mechanism, and the others link to it')
scope_entries.finding: Upstream records that six documents drifting apart is how stale promises reached diagnosing readers; the CLI's docs adopt the same discipline toward upstream — link, don't restate.

scope_entries.surface: local environment probes (nvidia-smi, which cargo/hf/uv, hf auth whoami, bluetoothctl devices, ~/.ssh, env)
scope_entries.finding: GB10 + CUDA 13 present; hf logged in; cargo present; no wandb netrc; BT sees only a mouse and a keyboard; no ssh hosts or /etc/hosts entries for a duck; no DUCK_* env. Training locally is feasible; reaching the duck needs its address.

scope_entries.surface: microduck sim-remote-io: docs/design/simulation.md + scripts/duck-sim + robotd/src/main.rs Args
scope_entries.finding: scripts/duck-sim encodes the three unguessable steps (policy paths in a params file, ORT dlopen from the RL venv, a <108-byte socket path) and env knobs DUCK_SIM_STATE/RL/PORT/DUCKS/SCENE/CAMERAS/DUCK. robotd args: --socket, --params, --fake, --sim host:port (conflicts with --fake), --no-policy, --unhealthy, --busy. duck-sim kills by pidfile + /proc check because a group kill once took out a login session.

scope_entries.surface: reachy-mini-cli reachy/behavior/{engine,rule_engine,model,sense,liveness,senselog}.py + CLAUDE.md single-SDK-owner + neurosymbolic-system CLAUDE.md seams
scope_entries.finding: Donor invariants: one tick seam, consumers never import engine internals, senses are injected peeks, rules are data, drop-don't-block on the tick budget (measured 425–1213 ms client construction is forbidden on the tick thread), heartbeat not flag files. neurosymbolic-system's brief lists exactly the seams to keep pure: TargetSink, SenseProviders, speech(text), media_session_provider, start_pose_provider.

scope_entries.surface: reachy-mini-cli CLAUDE.md 'behavior noun' (KindRegistry, goto_intent, intents spool, bounded-lifetime invariant) + duck-ipc-proto intent split
scope_entries.finding: The donor registers rule defaults and agent kinds (goto, mute/unmute, lock_face) into ONE registry at composition so 'behavior goto' and an agent's call share admission; unbounded looping admissions are refused on both surfaces. robotd's intents are already last-writer-wins and expiring, which suits a tick-driven emitter.

scope_entries.surface: microduck_rl pyproject.toml [tool.uv.sources] torch comment + scripts/hf/README.md + local nvidia-smi
scope_entries.finding: Upstream routes torch to the cu129 index only for linux-aarch64 and explains it by DGX Spark/GB10; Jetson boards are aarch64 too but run JetPack's CUDA/torch builds, which the file never mentions — untested territory. HF Jobs auto-forwards a wandb key only if present.

scope_entries.surface: microduck-cli CLAUDE.md 'neurosymbolic-system — the intended runtime (not usable yet)' + cicd SKILL.md triage defaults
scope_entries.finding: Both currently tell a reviewer that an engine loop in microduck_cli/ is a false-positive class to reject; that guidance must move with the decision.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / overlooked-actors + concurrency lens: duck-ipc-proto (robot.move as last-writer-wins notification, pad.input, robot.remoteSessionActive) + architecture.md 'padd sends the same intents an app would'
scope_entries.finding: Nothing in robotd distinguishes two writers; robotctl monitor shows asked-vs-applied but not who asked. In sim there is no padd unless started, so the hazard is invisible until a real duck or a console session.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / lifecycle lens: duck-ipc-proto ROBOT_ENABLE docstring + cheatsheet.md 'The robot must be driving for a skill to run' + duckctl.md 'do'
scope_entries.finding: c7's gated list omitted enable; the driving precondition for skills is documented three times upstream and would otherwise surface as a silent no-op in the rules layer.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / adjacent-systems lens: cheatsheet.md 'Policies and skills' + duckctl.md 'The skills array is the answer to what can this robot be asked for… read it before offering a button'
scope_entries.finding: Skills are config that differs per robot and per official-set tag; the console asks robot.policies rather than guessing, and a bound-but-missing skill is marked in the listing.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / reversibility lens: policy-channel-design.md §3 ('robotd writes the key, not the caller'; ephemeral try-mode rejected) + architecture.md state table
scope_entries.finding: Four processes edit robotd.toml under a lock; a fifth writer bypassing robotd would recreate the ephemeral-mode bug upstream removed. In sim the params file is generated by our env noun BEFORE robotd starts, which is the one legitimate write.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / failure-modes lens: arm101 release-on-abnormal-exit + duck-ipc-proto (ROBOT_POSE active:false, ROBOT_MOUTH per-tick, ROBOT_SOUND hold semantics, ROBOT_STOP 'not go limp') + cheatsheet deadman
scope_entries.finding: Continuous intents expire on their own; discrete state (a pose lean, a sound ride) needs an explicit release. Upstream's deadman covers velocity only.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / concurrency lens: reachy-mini-cli SpeechActuator (O(1) on tick, depth-2 queue, named drops) + robotd sim.rs TIMEOUT rationale ('a wedged simulator must not wedge the control loop') + architecture.md §2.2 'async with timeouts everywhere'
scope_entries.finding: One socket carries both correlated requests and uncorrelated notifications; the donor's measured lesson is that anything blocking on the tick thread is a 21–61x budget overrun.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / migration + upgrade lens: duck-ipc-proto API_VERSION skew rule ('a client pinned to v17 gets METHOD_NOT_FOUND naming the method — designed skew behaviour') + sim.rs PROTOCOL handshake
scope_entries.finding: No schema of ours lives on the duck; the only skew surfaces are API_VERSION (JSON-RPC) and the body protocol (duck-body↔robotd, not ours). Honesty condition added on c4.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / overlooked-actors lens: simulation.md §1 ('duck-sim up 4', named ducks, one machine-id each) + §4 faking the radio (duck-ether, 'designed and measured but not built')
scope_entries.finding: Upstream's twin is explicitly multi-duck; the ether is unbuilt. Scoping v1 to one engine per socket keeps the single-owner model the donor learned.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / lifecycle lens: reachy-mini-cli library.py feel-alive (PASSIVE base) + roadmap M9 ('a duck left alone in a room does something worth watching for ten minutes')
scope_entries.finding: Upstream's own definition of done for autonomy is idle liveliness; with no upstream brain today the engine's base behaviour is what makes an armed duck look alive.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / failure-modes lens: default_rules.toml preamble (three rules, ids are public, corroborated fields only) + cheatsheet 'fall is a report, not a gate' + [safety] fall_limp/fall_recover + BATTERY_EMPTY_V countdown
scope_entries.finding: robotd reports a fall but by default does not gate on it; the daemon sits the robot down at BATTERY_EMPTY_V. A rules layer that keeps firing skills into a fallen or dying duck is the obvious failure.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / security lens: remote-access-design.md §2.5 (a token in robotd.toml would appear in configure --list, the editor and the changes report) + local env (HF_TOKEN is set on this box) + duck-sim's pidfile-by-cmdline logic
scope_entries.finding: Upstream's lesson is that any diagnostic surface that prints config prints the secret; our doctor and --json outputs are exactly such surfaces.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / operations + security lens: architecture.md §2.2 SO_PEERCRED + allow_uids/allow_gids; reachy-mini-cli 'service' noun
scope_entries.finding: Sim sockets are user-owned so this is invisible today; parked for the first board.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / observability lens: cheatsheet 'robotctl monitor --json --hz 50 > run.jsonl' (one object per line, whole state) + reachy-mini-cli export/JSONL purity rule + parked v4
scope_entries.finding: Upstream already streams the whole state as NDJSON; recording it is the cheapest way to make rules testable without a daemon and to derive sense fields from evidence.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / migration lens: reachy-mini-cli rules.py (no schema_version today; per-id overlay merge) + decision c20 (engine extracted later)
scope_entries.finding: The planned extraction is a migration of operator-authored data; the donor's file has no version field, and the refactor would otherwise have nothing to key on.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / cheap-probes lens: rustc --version, PyPI onnxruntime 1.24.4 file list, CONTRIBUTING.md host build section
scope_entries.finding: Both prerequisites the sim launcher depends on are present here; a full build was not attempted (probes are read-only).

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / reversibility lens: every durable duck-side change is upstream's (policy load → robotd.toml, pad bind, configure) with an upstream undo (policy reset, pad reset, u in configure); ours are local files (rules overlay, recordings, state dir)
scope_entries.finding: Clean pass: nothing this CLI writes on the duck lacks an upstream undo; residual risk is only the durability surprise c34-style wording covers.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / data-loss lens: the train lane's artifacts (checkpoints in logs/, wandb runs, HF repos) are owned by microduck_rl / HF; the CLI records references, never moves or deletes them; publish refuses to overwrite an existing .onnx without --force upstream
scope_entries.finding: Clean pass: no user data surface of ours; residual risk is a --force passed through blindly — the CLI must not default it.
